# courtr

Courtr is a tool designed to assist with courtroom studies. It provides
customizable figures and a study template using R Shiny, which includes
a recordable notepad for participant notes, as well as color-coded
speech bubbles.

## Acknowledgements

This work was funded (or partially funded) by the Center for Statistics
and Applications in Forensic Evidence (CSAFE) through Cooperative
Agreements 70NANB15H176 and 70NANB20H019 between NIST and Iowa State
University, which includes activities carried out at Carnegie Mellon
University, Duke University, University of California Irvine, University
of Virginia, West Virginia University, University of Pennsylvania,
Swarthmore College and University of Nebraska, Lincoln.

Thank you to Richy Meleus for developing the cartoon figures used in
this app.

## Installation

You can install the development version of courtr from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("rachelesrogers/courtr")
```

## Getting Started

We recommend to start by using the
[`Save_Template()`](https://rachelesrogers.github.io/courtr/reference/Save_Template.md)
function to save the study template to your device. The README.txt file
in the study template provides detailed instructions on how to customize
the R Shiny application. To get an idea of what the study format looks
like, you can run the template without any modifications.

``` r
library(courtr)
```

``` r
Save_Template("your/file/path")
```

The testimony page of the app will look like this: ![template
screenshot](reference/figures/template_screenshot.png)

Insert your own testimony into the “Combined_Testimony.csv” file. Then,
use the
[`Format_Testimony()`](https://rachelesrogers.github.io/courtr/reference/Format_Testimony.md)
to format the testimony with the appropriate tags necessary for creating
the visual output. Save this formatted file as
“Combined_Testimony_Formatted.csv” in your downloaded template.

``` r

unformatted_testimony <- utils::read.csv("your/file/path/Combined_Testimony.csv")
formatted_testimony <- Format_Testimony(unformatted_testimony)

write.csv(formatted_testimony, "your/file/path/Combined_Testimony_Formatted.csv")
```

The characters used in the study can also be customized using the
[`Edit_Figures()`](https://rachelesrogers.github.io/courtr/reference/Edit_Figures.md)
function. This function will pull up an R Shiny app, allowing for
customization of provided figures. The figures can be downloaded and
saved in “your/file/path/www” to be used in your study.

``` r
Edit_Figures()
```

![editing screenshot](reference/figures/figure_edits.png)

# Package index

## All functions

- [`Edit_Figures()`](https://rachelesrogers.github.io/courtr/reference/Edit_Figures.md)
  : Edit Color of Cartoon Figures
- [`Format_Testimony()`](https://rachelesrogers.github.io/courtr/reference/Format_Testimony.md)
  : Format Testimony
- [`Save_Template()`](https://rachelesrogers.github.io/courtr/reference/Save_Template.md)
  : Save RShiny Courtroom Study Template
- [`figure_information`](https://rachelesrogers.github.io/courtr/reference/figure_information.md)
  : Information on Figure Characteristics and Default Colors
